nodes.summary: For a positive integer $k$, the $k$-th sine basis function is $u_k : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $u_k(x) = \sqrt{2} \sin(k\pi x)$.
nodes.title: Sine basis functions on $(0, 1)$

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $k$, the $k$-th element $b_k$ of the sine Hilbert basis of $L^2([0, 1])$ satisfies $b_k(x) = \sqrt{2} \sin(k\pi x)$ for almost every $x \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The sine Hilbert basis consists of sine functions

nodes.summary: The sine Hilbert basis is a Hilbert basis $(b_k)_{k \ge 1}$ of the real Hilbert space $L^2([0, 1])$, indexed by the positive integers, with $b_k(x) = \sqrt{2} \sin(k\pi x)$ for almost every $x \in [0, 1]$. Such a basis exists, and since an element of $L^2([0, 1])$ is determined by its values almost everywhere, it is unique.
nodes.title: The sine Hilbert basis of $L^2((0, 1))$

nodes.summary: The canonical sine basis is orthonormal on the unit interval, in product-integral form.
nodes.title: Orthonormality of the sine basis on the unit interval

nodes.summary: The Green's eigenvalues $\lambda_k = 1/(k^2\pi^2)$ tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter on the positive integers, that is, $\lambda_k \to 0$ as $k \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The Green's eigenvalues tend to zero

nodes.summary: For the Green's eigenvalues $\lambda_k = 1/(k^2\pi^2)$, indexed by the positive integers $k$, we have $\sum_{k \ge 1} \lambda_k^2 = 1/90$.
